requirement: Generate numeric one-time login codes with a cryptographic RNG and verify them with a hard limit on attempts and single use.
skeleton: Digit and attempt constants, an OtpLockedError, generate_code validating the digit count and zero-padding randbelow, and an OtpChallenge with remaining and a check that locks, counts, and compares in constant time.
caption: Numeric one-time codes drawn with secrets and checked with hmac under an attempt limit. OtpLockedError is a plain Exception. generate_code(digits=6) raises ValueError saying digits must be between 4 and 10 outside that range, and otherwise returns secrets.randbelow(10**digits) formatted zero-padded to the digit count. OtpChallenge(code) tracks attempts and whether it was used; remaining returns zero once used, else MAX_ATTEMPTS of 3 minus the attempts. check raises OtpLockedError saying challenge closed when used or out of attempts, counts the attempt, and when hmac.compare_digest of the encoded strings matches marks it used and returns True, else False. The fixture asserts six digit codes, zero padding and the randbelow bound through a fake, digit validation, one accepted use, locking after three wrong tries, and a compare_digest call on bytes.

plan.intent: Send and verify SMS login codes
constraints: Codes come from secrets.randbelow(10**digits) and are zero padded
Digit counts outside 4 to 10 raise ValueError
A correct code is accepted once
Three wrong attempts lock the challenge

rationale.teaches: Draw codes with randbelow over the full range, pad with a format spec, and gate checks on used and attempt counters before a constant-time compare.
rationale.why: Unpadded codes shrink the keyspace and leak their shape, and unlimited or reusable attempts let a six digit code be brute forced in minutes.

ops.docstring: Numeric one-time codes from secrets.randbelow with an attempt limit.

ops.source:
class OtpLockedError(Exception):
    """Raised when a challenge was already used or ran out of attempts."""

candidates.why_wrong: Small random values produce codes shorter than the requested digit count.
A fourth guess is allowed after the three attempt limit.
An accepted code stays usable and can log in again.
Codes are compared with == which short-circuits and leaks timing.
Too few digits are accepted, producing trivially guessable codes.
